purpose: One approved real-time kernel trace of the original failed-PR test EXE, without recording a general desktop ETL

officialReferences.supports: Real-time sessions have no log filename; handlers consume kernel events, buffered callbacks can arrive after event generation.
System-provider schema has keywords/stacks/pool tags; a user-mode ProcessExeFilter must not be advertised as a kernel process whitelist.
PID scope filter is not a generic solution for kernel-mode providers and dynamically born child processes.
Process/loader, scheduler/context-switch and IO categories are system logger events.
Pinned Microsoft TraceEvent decoder package; official metadata SHA512 independently verified, not globally installed.

privilegeRequirement: The prepared entry point requires a manually elevated controller and an explicit approval switch; ordinary-token rejection was tested.
futureCaptureAcceptanceRequirements: Actual failing query-case output, not the separate license.opened failure or a success comparison.
Original failing case/control PID bound to ETW process generation and API creation/image observation when available.
Owned Node ProcessStart/Stop, thread lifecycle, ready/context-switch and useful loader/FileIO events cover the failure window.
Unrelated event payloads, command lines, SIDs and scheduling counterpart IDs must not be serialized.
Root-start seen, consumer/writer drain and owned-session stop succeed; decoded errors or dropped records invalidate full coverage.
Report kernel loss count as a pre-stop snapshot, not as proof of zero loss through final shutdown.
Preserve original default concurrency/capture/deadlines and any failures, even if the failing CI case does not reproduce.
Keep the original failure and version gates open unless evidence actually establishes their resolution.
